source.author: stat
source.text: si bene quid merui, si me de matre cadentem fovisti gremio et traiectum vulnere plantas firmasti, si stagna peti Cirrhaea bicorni interfusa iugo, possem cum degere falso contentus Polybo, trifidaeque in Phocidos arto longaevum implicui regem secuique frementis ora senis, dum quaero patrem, si Sphingos iniquae callidus ambages te praemonstrante resolvi, si dulces furias et lamentabile matris conubium gavisus ini noctemque nefandam saepe tuli natosque tibi, seis ipsa, paravi, mox avidus poenae digitis eaedentibus ultro incubui miseraque oculos in matre reliqui:
source.text_original: si bene quid merui, si me de matre cadentem / fovisti gremio et traiectum vulnere plantas / firmasti, si stagna peti Cirrhaea bicorni / interfusa iugo, possem cum degere falso / contentus Polybo, trifidaeque in Phocidos arto / longaevum implicui regem secuique frementis / ora senis, dum quaero patrem, si Sphingos iniquae / callidus ambages te praemonstrante resolvi, / si dulces furias et lamentabile matris / conubium gavisus ini noctemque nefandam / saepe tuli natosque tibi, seis ipsa, paravi, / mox avidus poenae digitis eaedentibus ultro / incubui miseraque oculos in matre reliqui: /
source.text_english: if I have deserved anything well, if you cherished me, fallen from my mother’s womb, in your lap and, pierced by a wound, steadied my feet, if I reached the Cirrhaean marshes lying between the twin peaks, when I could have lived content with false Polybus, and in the narrow pass of Phocis I entangled the long-lived king and cut through the fierce mouth of the old man while I sought my father; if, with you showing the way, I cleverly unraveled the twists of the cruel Sphinx; if I joyfully entered upon sweet madness and my mother’s lamentable marriage, and often endured that unholy night, and prepared children for you, as you yourself know; then soon, eager for punishment, I of my own accord fell upon those clawing fingers, and I left my eyes behind in my wretched mother’s body:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_original: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde / occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes / dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem / Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, / segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_english: From here Telamon holds the sea to the left; from there Alcides occupies the other sea from a higher place. The rest of the young men are divided: swift Asterion, whom Piresius, his father, as he was falling, nourished with twin rivers, and slower Enipeus, where he feels the strength of the Apidanus.
